gallery_summary.total_assets_scope: Thousands of digitized folios, paintings, and historical artifacts spanning the 11th to 20th centuries.
gallery_summary.primary_focus: Illuminated manuscripts from the two main Jain sects (Digambara and Śvetāmbara), detailing cosmology, monastic rules, and the lives of the Tīrthaṅkaras.

compositional_elements: Protruding eyes (characteristic of Western Indian style)

collection_sources.holdings_type: Extensive collections of the Kalpa-sūtra and Saṅgrahaṇī-sūtra manuscripts containing rich cosmic diagrams.
Rich array of fabric paintings, structural temple hangings (Pata), and metal shrine sculptures.
Early palm-leaf works and rare texts featuring heavily decorated margins and stylized geometric shapes.
Focus on medical, astrological, and palmistry texts mixed with traditional Jain concepts.

visual_subjects: The 14 or 16 auspicious dreams of Queen Triśalā preceding Mahāvīra's birth.
Renunciation scenes (Kesa-loca) where kings pluck out their hair to become monks.
Attainment of omniscience (Kevala-jñāna) under sacred trees.
Maps of the middle world (Madhyaloka) showing concentric rings of oceans and continents.
Detailed structures of the universe shaped like a cosmic giant (Lokapuruṣa).
The universal assembly hall (Samavasaraṇa) where a Jina sits to preach to all living beings.
Yantras and Mandalas used for daily meditation and esoteric sound formulas.
Footprints (Pādukā) of liberated souls carved into stone mounts.
Laypersons performing the ritual anointment (Abhiṣeka) of monolithic statues.
